podcast.body: Released in 1973, "Jolene" became a number one hit on the country charts and is Dolly's most covered song. It represents a plea from a woman to a beautiful rival not to take her man, contrasting with Loretta Lynn's more confrontational songs like "Fist City." The lyrics vividly describe Jolene's beauty and the narrator's desperation. "Jolene, number one on the country charts in 1973 that is Dolly's most covered song."

srcs.episode: Ep. 23 - Women of Country Music in the 70s

podcast.body: Released in Fall 1973, this song features a narrator pleading with another woman not to take her man. It was inspired by Dolly Parton's real-life husband flirting with a local bank clerk, while the visual image of Jolene came from a red-headed young fan with green eyes who asked for an autograph. It became a big hit for Parton, won a Grammy, and has been covered many times. "It was inspired when her real-life husband started flirting with a local bank clerk."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
